title: fix(cli)!: os migrate apply exits 1 when the confirmation it needs is not given
body:
Fixes #24949
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

`os migrate apply` now exits `1` when the confirmation it needs is not given (stdin is not a terminal, or `--json`, and no `--yes`), as every other `os migrate` subcommand with a confirmation gate already does. Nothing else about that run changes: it still applies nothing, prints the same warning and, under `--json`, emits the same document. An operator who answers `n` at the terminal prompt still gets exit `0`.

## Measured before the change (the CLI binary built at the branch base `e4d604efd3`)

The fixture is a config-only project on a SQLite file (`OS_DATABASE_URL`, `NODE_ENV=production`). It has one object whose `legacy_note` field was removed after a first `os migrate apply --yes`, so `os migrate plan` lists one destructive change, `os24949_thing.legacy_note [drop_column]`. A `safe drift` copy instead declares one new field (an `add_column`). For `recorded-by` and `resume`, a copy was seeded with one sentinel history row and one interrupted journal run, so each run reaches its gate. `organization-ownership` was given a plan file its own plan run wrote. "Written" compares a content hash of the schema plus every row of every table, read on a separate connection before and after each run. It is never a file hash. The terminal column used a real pseudo-terminal that answered `n` at the `[y/N]` prompt.

| subcommand, writing mode, no `--yes` | stdin `/dev/null` | `--json` | terminal, answered `n` | written |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `apply --allow-destructive` | **0** | **0** | 0 | nothing (the column is still there) |
| `apply` (safe drift) | **0** | **0** | n/a | nothing |
| `activity-changed-fields --apply` | 1 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| `audit-mail-bodies --apply` | 1 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| `audit-metadata-bodies --apply` | 1 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| `comment-parent-pair --apply` | 1 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| `comment-reactions --apply` | 1 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| `files-to-references --apply` | 1 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| `meta --stored --apply` | 1 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| `multi-value-columns --apply` | 1 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| `recorded-by --apply` | 1 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| `resume --run RUN` | 1 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| `security-catalog-overlays --apply` | 1 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| `summary-nulls --apply` | 1 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| `value-shapes --apply` | 1 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| `organization-ownership --apply --plan-file PLAN` (no `--backup-taken`) | 1 | 1 | 1 | nothing |

- Every non-interactive run printed a line naming its confirmation flag: `--yes` for every row except the last, which names `--backup-taken`. No run wrote anything without its confirmation.
- `apply` was the only member answering 0. `summary-nulls` and `value-shapes` were not in the claim's candidate list. They have `--yes` gates too and were measured as control rows.
- **Detection is one rule across the family.** Every gate is `flags.json || !process.stdin.isTTY`, and every `confirm()` returns false on a non-TTY stdin before it builds a prompt. No CI variable is read, `apply` included. The divergence was only the exit.
- `recorded-by --apply` and `resume --run` gate after a plain boot. Re-measured on a copy whose config was one field ahead of the database, the content hash was unchanged: that boot added no column.

## The change

- `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts`: the text face now ends with `this.exit(1)` after its warning. The `--json` face emits its document with exit `1` (`emitJson(…, 1); return;`), which is the spelling `apply`'s own three refusals already use, so the one-shot exit at the end of `run()` leaves with it. The warning text and the document are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **Route.** No shared helper or named exit constant exists for this. Each sibling spells it inline (`printWarning(…); this.exit(1)`), and `CliExitCode` in `src/utils/format.ts` is `0 | 1`. A new helper adopted by the 14 sites would rewrite 13 that are already right. The pin below holds the family to one code instead, and its population is discovered.

## The pin: `packages/cli/test/migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts` (unit tier)

- **Population, discovered.** Every module under `src/commands/migrate` whose command class declares a `yes` or `apply` flag. That is 15 members, and the roster must equal them. A future subcommand with a confirmation gate fails the first case by id until its row is added.
- **Per member, both faces**, with `process.stdin.isTTY` set to false by the case itself: exit `1`, the text face names the member's confirmation flag, and no write seam is reached. For members that gate before the boot, the write seam is the boot. For `apply` it is `flushSchemaDdl` / `applyMigrationEntries`, and for `recorded-by` / `resume` the journal runner.
- **Controls.** `apply --allow-destructive --yes` applies and exits `0`. `apply` on a terminal answered `n` asks the prompt once, writes nothing and exits `0`.
- **Replaced seams:** the occupancy probe, the boot, the journal runner and reads, the sentinel scan, the one-shot exit and readline. The parse, the gates, `emitJson` and `this.exit` run for real. The commands are imported from `src/`, so no `dist/` sits on the resolution path.

Evidence:

- **Red on `main`.** `apply.ts` was restored from the base into the tree only (tree blob `091e6bb` equals the base blob). The pin ran 2 failed, 32 passed: `apply — text face` and `apply — --json face`, each `expected +0 to be 1`. The restore was `git checkout HEAD`, and the blob `5581f5d` equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` is empty and `git status` is clean.
- **Green on the branch:** 34 passed.
- **Ablations** through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. Each mutation was proven on disk (anchor 1 → 0, blob changed) and restored hash-equal to HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty:
  - removing `apply`'s text-face `this.exit(1)` → 1 failed (`apply — text face`), 33 passed;
  - `apply`'s `--json` exit `1` → `0` → 1 failed (`apply — --json face`), 33 passed;
  - removing `comment-reactions`'s text-face `this.exit(1)` → 1 failed (`comment-reactions — text face`), 33 passed. The per-member rows hold the siblings, not only `apply`.
  - A first attempt at the text-face ablation was refused by the tool before any test ran. Its replacement was a substring of the anchor, so the replacement count could not rise. The file was restored hash-equal and the ablation was re-run with a marked replacement. The first attempt was a no-op and is not counted.

## After, at the public door (the CLI built from this branch)

| command | exit | written |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `apply --allow-destructive`, stdin `/dev/null` | 1 | nothing; the same `⚠ Confirmation required …` line |
| `apply --allow-destructive --json` | 1 | nothing; `message: confirmation_required`, `hint: pass --yes` |
| `apply` (safe drift), stdin `/dev/null` | 1 | nothing |
| `apply --allow-destructive`, terminal answered `n` | 0 | nothing; `Aborted — no changes made.` |
| `apply --allow-destructive --yes` (control) | 0 | the column dropped; `✓ Applied 1 change(s).` |

## Local verification (final head `5a3e45078e`)

- `@objectstack/cli` unit tier (`vitest run --project unit`): 316 files, 4684 tests passed, at `ddd7dfdb62`. The only later commit is a type cast in the new test file, and that file re-ran green at `5a3e45078e` (34 passed).
- Integration tier declared to CI: the diff touches no integration-tier file and no spawn entry. The one integration file whose run reaches `apply`'s gate (`plan.reads-env-files.integration.test.ts`, which reads the document and not the exit) was run anyway: 6 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck: OK`). The first run flagged one TS2352 in the new test file, fixed in `5a3e45078e`.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 68 commands, and its 11 declared WIDE-population families were run too, 79 in all. 77 exited 0 on the first pass. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`: no `dist/` for packages this diff does not touch). After a workspace build both exited 0. `--ran` printed `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 68 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main`: exit 0, `✓ This diff introduces no major bump.`
- `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base e4d604efd3`: exit 0. It lists `24949-migrate-apply-confirmation-exit.md [BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
- `pnpm lint` (the whole repository, `eslint . --no-inline-config`): exit 0.

Changeset: `.changeset/24949-migrate-apply-confirmation-exit.md`, `@objectstack/cli` `minor`, with a **BREAKING** banner, the FROM → TO, what is unchanged, the one-line script fix (pass `--yes`, or run `os migrate plan` to preview) and its ADR-0087 disposition. Clause-② narrowing means a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review of record is owed before the queue.

## Acceptance notes

- **`organization-ownership`'s terminal decline exits 1; every other member's exits 0.** Its prompt asks whether a backup was taken, and a `n` there is the refusal "--apply needs a backup of this database first". This was measured and left as it is: an interactive decline keeps its code, and that is a hold-off of this card. No carrier.
- **Docs that still say exit 0.** `content/docs/upgrading.mdx` (the v18.0.0 step 8) and `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx` (the 18.0.0 checklist, from #24922: "read the output, not the exit code") say a non-interactive `apply` without `--yes` still exits `0`. Both describe the measured 18.0.0 walk, which stays true of 18.0.0. The release page is release-owned and is not edited in a code PR. The behaviour change reaches the next release's notes through this changeset. Carrier: the release compilation (maintainer).
- **`apply`'s `--json` document names the condition in `message`, where its siblings use `error`.** The document shape is a hold-off of this card, and it is unchanged. Noted only.
- `main` moved 5 commits past the base while this ran, none of them under `packages/cli`. The branch was not merged with it.
